requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A business will have taxable transactions in Florida (selling taxable goods or certain taxable services, e.g., restaurant sales of prepared food) and must register as a sales and use tax dealer before beginning business in Florida.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 212

forms.name: Florida Business Tax Application (Form DR-1)
Certificate of Registration (Form DR-11)
Florida Annual Resale Certificate for Sales Tax (Form DR-13)

requirements.notes: Register online through the Department's website application interview, or by paper DR-1 if no internet access. After approval, the Department issues the DR-11 (must be displayed in a visible place at the business location), the DR-13 for tax-exempt purchases intended for resale, and filing information. Dealers collect sales tax at the time of each sale, remit with Form DR-15 for each reporting period, and must file a return even if no tax is due. The online system guides applicants through determining their tax obligations.
requirements.title: Sales and Use Tax Dealer Registration (Certificate of Registration, DR-11)

requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A restaurant, cafe, or similar food business sells food or drinks cooked or prepared on the seller's premises and sold ready for immediate consumption (on or off premises). This is the core restaurant trigger for sales-and-use-tax dealer registration.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 212.08(1); Fla. Admin. Code R. 12A-1.011(5)

forms.name: Florida Business Tax Application (Form DR-1)

requirements.notes: The Department's position: the grocery exemption in s. 212.08(1) does not cover foods or drinks cooked or prepared on the seller's premises and sold ready for immediate consumption (Rule 12A-1.011(5) defines this as food normally cooked, prepared, served, or sold by restaurants, cafes, lunch counters, cafeterias, etc.). Food sold heated, with eating utensils provided, maintained at elevated temperature (heat lamps, warming trays), or sold on platters/as dinners is taxable. Such sales are taxable transactions requiring DR-1 dealer registration before the business begins operating.
requirements.title: Restaurant prepared-food sales are taxable transactions (trigger for DR-1 dealer registration)

requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A dealer sells or delivers taxable goods or taxable services into a Florida county that imposes a discretionary sales surtax.
requirements.citation: Fla. Admin. Code R. 12A-15.002

forms.name: Sales and Use Tax Return (Form DR-15)

requirements.notes: Most Florida counties impose a discretionary sales surtax that generally applies to transactions subject to sales and use tax. The dealer must collect surtax at the rate imposed in the county where the goods or services are delivered, and remit it to the Department together with sales and use tax on the DR-15. The surtax applies to the first $5,000 of any single item of tangible personal property; the $5,000 cap does not apply to admissions, transient rentals, or services.
requirements.title: Discretionary sales surtax collection (county local-option surtax)

requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A registered dealer paid more than $1,000 in sales and use tax during the most recent state fiscal year (July 1 - June 30).
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 212.12; Fla. Admin. Code R. 12A-1.056, 12A-12.004

forms.name: Sales and Use Tax Return (Form DR-15)

requirements.notes: RESOLVED 2026-10-13: official DOR tiers — monthly if annual tax >$1,000; quarterly if ≤$1,000; semiannual if <$500 over four consecutive quarters; annual if ≤$100 over four quarters (s. 212.11(1)(c)). Mandatory e-filing threshold is $5,000 (current DR-15N instructions, R. 10/25); the $30,000 figure in older DOR TIPs is outdated. Confirmed on floridarevenue.com. Original note: DOR's publication confirms only the >$1,000 annual-tax monthly-filing trigger (s. 212.12). The finer filing-frequency tiers for smaller dealers (annual/semiannual/quarterly) were seen in third-party summaries but not confirmed on an official DOR page; see open_questions.
requirements.timeline: Monthly tax returns are due on or before the 20th day of each month following the collection period (first business day after the 20th if the 20th falls on a weekend or state/federal holiday).
requirements.title: Sales and use tax filing frequency (monthly filing threshold)

requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A business meets any liability criterion: (a) $1,500 quarterly payroll, or employs at least one worker for a day or portion of a day for 20 weeks in a calendar year (includes corporate officer wages, draws, dividends, distributions); (b) is a government entity; (c) has a 501(c)(3) exemption and employs 4+ workers for a day or portion of a day for 20 weeks; (d) employs agricultural labor with 5+ workers for a day or portion of a day for 20 weeks or pays $10,000+ cash in any quarter; (e) employs domestic workers paying $1,000+ cash in any quarter; (f) acquired a liable employer's business; (g) must pay federal unemployment taxes; or (h) voluntarily elects coverage.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 443

forms.name: Florida Business Tax Application (Form DR-1)
Employer's Quarterly Report (Form RT-6)

requirements.notes: A liable employer must register to report Florida reemployment tax; DOR assigns a seven-digit reemployment tax account number. Employers must file the Employer's Quarterly Report (RT-6) each quarter regardless of employment activity or whether any tax is due (domestic employers may qualify for annual filing). Workers pay none of this tax; employers may not deduct it from payroll. Registration is completed via the DR-1 application (online interview at floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration).
requirements.title: Reemployment tax employer registration

requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A registered employer owes reemployment tax on employee wages.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 443

forms.name: Reemployment Tax Rate Notice (Form RT-20)

requirements.notes: New liable employers start at an initial rate of 0.0270 (2.7%), held until the employer has reported for 10 quarters; the rate is then experience-rated on benefits charged vs. taxable payroll. By law the rate may not fall below 0.0010 (0.1%; $7 per employee effective 1/1/2026) and the maximum is 0.0540 (5.4%; $378 per employee). Only the first $7,000 of wages paid to each employee in a calendar year is taxable. Employers with stable employment records receive reduced rates after a qualifying period.
requirements.timeline: Rate notices mailed to all contributing employers each year; protests of a rate determination must be filed in writing within 20 days of the 'Mailed On or Before' date on Form RT-20.
requirements.title: Reemployment tax rates and taxable wage base

requirements.agency: County property appraiser (Florida Department of Revenue form DR-405)
requirements.applies_when: A business (restaurant included) owns tangible personal property used for commercial purposes on January 1, such as furniture, fixtures, computers, tools, supplies, machines, kitchen equipment, and leasehold improvements — property not included in the assessed value of the business's real property.
requirements.citation: Florida Department of Revenue, Instructions for Form DR-405 (R. 01/18); Fla. Stat. ss. 193.052, 196.183

forms.name: Tangible Personal Property Tax Return (Form DR-405)

requirements.notes: RESOLVED 2026-10-13: official DOR property-tax page confirms 25% failure-to-file penalty, 5%/month late-filing penalty (capped at 25%), 15% for unlisted property — matching s. 193.072. Original note: Each DR-405 is eligible for an exemption of up to $25,000 of assessed value; filing on time automatically applies for the exemption, and Florida law provides for loss of the exemption if not filed on time. Report summary totals on page 1 with an itemized list (original cost and date acquired) attached. File a separate return for each site in the county where the business transacts business. This is an ad valorem tax assessed locally — DOR provides the form; the county property appraiser administers it.
requirements.timeline: Return must be filed with the county property appraiser's office by April 1 each year. A 30-day extension is granted on request; the property appraiser may grant an additional 15 days. The extension must be requested in time for the property appraiser to act before April 1.
requirements.title: Tangible personal property tax return (business fixtures/equipment)

requirements.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
requirements.applies_when: A corporation or entity does business, earns or receives income, or exists in Florida, including out-of-state corporations doing business in Florida.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 220

forms.name: Florida Corporate Income/Franchise Tax Return (Form F-1120)

requirements.notes: Must file a Florida corporate income tax return even if no tax is due. S corporations and tax-exempt organizations do not file if they have no federal taxable income, but must file and pay any tax due if they do. Homeowner/condominium associations filing federal Form 1120-H do not file; those filing federal Form 1120 must. Keep light per scope: one entry only.
requirements.title: Corporate income tax return (C-corporations)

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Any person planning to open or operating a place in Florida that prepares, serves, or sells food to the public (restaurants, cafes, bars/lounges with food service, take-out/delivery operations, mall and food-court food service, etc.). Exclusions: operations regulated by FDACS or DOH (e.g., schools, hospitals), churches/civic nonprofits serving members, common-carrier food service (planes/trains), and places serving only ice, beverages, popcorn, or prepackaged items.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.241

forms.name: DBPR HR-7030 — Application for Fixed Public Food Service Establishment License with Plan Review (combination packet)
DBPR HR-7035 — Application for Fixed Public Food Service Establishment License (no plan review)
DBPR HR-7007 — Application for Public Food Service Establishment License

requirements.notes: Owners of new public food service establishments, and new owners of existing establishments, must obtain a license from the division BEFORE commencing operation. Each operation requires a separate license (e.g., a hotel restaurant needs its own food service license in addition to the hotel's lodging license). DBPR inspection records quote s. 509.241(1): 'Each public lodging and public food service establishment shall obtain a license from the division' and (2): 'Each person who plans to open a public food service establishment shall apply for and receive a license from the division prior to the commencement of operation.'
requirements.timeline: Most applications processed within a few business days when submitted online; allow additional time for mailed applications.
requirements.title: Public food service establishment license required before operating

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Applying for or renewing any DBPR public food service establishment license; fee depends on license type, seating capacity (for seating establishments), county/licensing district, and application timing.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ss. 509.251, 509.302; FAC Rule 61C-1.008 (fee schedule adopted by rule)
requirements.fees: Full-year / half-year fees as published: Permanent food service (Seating): Nonseating $242/$126; 1-49 seats $262/$136; 50-149 seats $273/$141.50; 150-249 seats $294/$152; 250-349 seats $315/$162.50; 350-499 seats $336/$173; 500+ seats $357/$183.50. Caterers $263/$136.50. Mobile Food Dispensing Vehicles / Hot Dog Carts / Temporary Commercial Kitchens $347/$178.50. Vending Machines $21/$15.50. Theme Park Food Carts $262-$357/$136-$183.50 by cart count. Temporary Food Vendors: annual $456, 1-3 day $91, 4-30 day $105. Plus: $50 one-time application fee for new or change-of-ownership applications (in addition to license fee); $10 Hospitality Education Program (HEP) fee included in the fees above and not prorated; plan review provided at no charge ($0).
requirements.notes: Fee schedule is adopted by rule (61C-1.008, FAC) as required by s. 509.251. Seating establishments report the number of seats available to the public; DBPR does not set seating limits (those are set by local building, fire, and water/sewer authorities).
requirements.title: License categories by seating/capacity and published fee schedule

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Every DBPR food service licensee; licenses are annual and expire on a fixed date per district regardless of when the application was submitted.
requirements.notes: Licenses are annual (not multi-year) and renewable online. State divided into 7 licensing districts by county with staggered expirations: District 1 (Miami region: Dade, Monroe) Oct 1; District 2 (Ft. Lauderdale region: Broward, Martin, Palm Beach) Dec 1; District 3 (Tampa region: Citrus, Hernando, Hillsborough, Pasco, Pinellas, Polk, Sumter) Feb 1; District 4 (Orlando region: Brevard, Indian River, Lake, Orange, Osceola, St. Lucie, Seminole, Volusia) Apr 1; District 5 (Jacksonville region) Jun 1; District 6 (Panama City region) Jun 1; District 7 (Ft. Myers region) Dec 1. Full-year fee applies if applying during the renewal period (~2 months before expiration) or more than 6 months before next renewal; half-year fee applies if applying 6 months or less before the next renewal period (HEP $10 not prorated). Renewal reminder notices are mailed about 60 days before expiration. A delinquent fee (prescribed by rule, capped at $50 by statute) applies to late renewals.
requirements.timeline: Annual; renewal reminders ~60 days before expiration.
requirements.title: License year and renewal cycle (7 staggered districts)

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Opening a new public food service establishment or taking ownership of an existing one in Florida.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 509; FAC Rule 61C-1.002

forms.name: DBPR Online Services account application (create account, apply online)
DBPR HR-7030 — license + plan review combination application

requirements.notes: Four published steps: (1) create a DBPR Online account; (2) apply for and complete plan review (food service licenses only); (3) apply for a license and pay the license fee; (4) schedule and pass the licensing (opening) inspection. Steps 1-3 can be completed online; the division recommends the combination (COMBO) application applying for license and plan review at the same time as the fastest path. Most applications are processed within a few business days once received; allow more time for mailed applications. Applicants are urged to also clear county/municipal requirements, obtain a Florida sales tax number, a federal EIN, and (if selling alcohol) a Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco license before significant financial commitments.
requirements.timeline: Most applications processed within a few business days; online plan review reviewed within 30 days of submission.
requirements.title: License application process (online account, plan review, fee, inspection)

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Plan review is required when the establishment is: (1) newly built, (2) converted from another use, (3) remodeled, or (4) reopened after being closed at least 18 months. Also required for permanent food service when an operator changes the menu in a way that requires different equipment or changes the overall operational concept. NO plan review is required for a change of ownership with no interruption in operation, construction, remodeling, or conversion; or when sharing an already DBPR-licensed kitchen with no changes.
requirements.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61C-1.002
requirements.fees: Plan review is provided at no charge ($0) per the published food service fee page.

forms.name: Plan review application (online via DBPR Online Services; printable forms via division forms center)
DBPR HR-7030 — license + plan review combination application

requirements.notes: Plan review applicants are encouraged to apply online. Required submittals: a complete application, a scale drawing of the floor plan with equipment labeled, and a sample menu (PDF preferred; high-quality plans drawn to scale). The division reviews online applications within 30 days and recommends plan review approval be completed before construction to avoid costly modifications. For remodels of an already DBPR-licensed establishment, link the license in an Online Services account and select 'Remodel Plan Review.' A variance may be requested in writing if plans do not meet sanitation/safety requirements (no fee; 90-day response for routine, 30-day for emergency).
requirements.timeline: Online plan review applications reviewed within 30 days of submission.
requirements.title: DBPR plan review for new construction, conversion, remodeling, or reopening

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Every new license requires a satisfactory opening inspection before the establishment may serve food to the public (vacation rentals excepted; this part covers restaurants only).
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 509; FAC Rule 61C-1.002
requirements.notes: After plan review approval, application, and fee payment, contact DBPR Customer Contact Center (850-487-1395) several business days before the opening date to schedule; inspectors do not routinely conduct pre-opening or courtesy inspections — do not call until absolutely ready. Do not serve food to the public until a satisfactory inspection and a license to operate are obtained. Have proof of other approvals onsite (building, electrical, fire, plumbing). After passing, the operator receives a temporary paper license on the spot. Change-of-ownership applications do not require an opening inspection if the previous owner received a satisfactory inspection within 120 days before the application is processed; otherwise an opening inspection is conducted after the new owner legally takes over.
requirements.title: Opening inspection required before operating

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: All licensed public food service establishments, for the life of the license.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.032 (inspection of premises; risk-based frequency adopted by rule)
requirements.notes: Routine inspections are unannounced. DBPR personnel inspect 'as often as necessary for enforcement of the provisions of law and rule, and the protection of the public's health, safety, and welfare,' and operators must permit right of entry at any reasonable time and make records available. Fla. Stat. s. 509.032 directs the division to adopt by rule a risk-based inspection frequency of at least 1 and no more than 4 routine inspections per year (considering inspection/compliance history, food type/preparation, and service type) — the statute's current text could not be fetched during this session (flsenate.gov timed out); confirm before quoting the 1-4 figure. Deficiencies are documented in inspection reports classified High Priority, Intermediate, or Basic, with references to the relevant regulation. Reports state when violations must be corrected (a date certain or by the next routine inspection); many violations are corrected on site. Division procedures compel compliance through follow-up visits, administrative action, or closure when necessary. Inspection reports are published publicly: DBPR's Licensing Portal 'View Food & Lodging Inspections' search shows detailed inspection reports (inspection type/date/result, violation counts and observations) for inspections after October 1, 2003. Establishments are not graded or rated.
requirements.timeline: Risk-based; at least 1 and no more than 4 routine inspections per year (pending direct statute confirmation).
requirements.title: Routine inspections and public inspection reports

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Public food service establishments in Florida — food managers must complete training and pass a certification exam within 30 days of employment.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.039; FAC Rule 61C-4.023

forms.name: DBPR Form HR 5030-080 — food manager certification cut-sheet handout (English/Spanish PDFs)

requirements.notes: Training and testing are provided by PRIVATE accredited entities, not by DBPR — DBPR approves/lists the programs (e.g., ServSafe/National Restaurant Association Educational Foundation, National Registry of Food Safety Professionals, 360training/Learn2Serve, State Food Safety, Always Food Safe, and others; ANAB-CFP is the accrediting body). All public food service establishments must provide the division with proof of food manager certification upon request, including at any division inspection. DBPR-published inspection standards cite a currently certified food service manager must be on duty when four or more employees are engaged in food preparation/handling (violation code 53A-05). Certification is valid 5 years (per ServSafe Florida regulatory summary; recertification by examination).
requirements.timeline: Training and exam completed within 30 days of employment.
requirements.title: Certified food manager requirement (private accredited providers)

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: All food service employees of Florida public food service establishments.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.049; FAC Rule 61C-4.023
requirements.notes: Florida requires all food service employees to be trained in proper food handling and hygiene practices every three years. Only division-approved training programs are accepted (the division maintains a Training Programs List of approved independent entities and states it is no longer accepting new applications for food safety training certification programs). In-house proprietary programs approved by DBPR and taught by the establishment's own certified food manager(s) are allowed. Third-party providers must maintain and electronically submit training data to DBPR per s. 509.049(7)(b). Establishments must provide proof of employee training on request, including at division inspections. DBPR HR-7030 — if plan review is triggered

requirements.notes: RESOLVED 2026-10-13: Rule 61C-1.002, F.A.C. is controlling — plan review is required for establishments reopened after being out of business for MORE THAN 18 MONTHS; change-of-ownership applications need no plan review when there is no interruption in operation or change to the establishment. The 'closed less than a year' language came from older DBPR form versions (HR-7007 era) and is superseded. Verified on current DBPR packet HR-7030 (May 2024) and the flrules.org rulemaking record. Apply for CHANGE OF OWNER when taking over a space currently licensed by a restaurant or where a restaurant closed less than a year ago (per the guide); apply for a NEW license if the space was never a restaurant or closed over 18 months ago. No plan review is required for change of ownership if there is no interruption in operation, construction, remodeling, or conversion; no opening inspection is required if the previous owner received a satisfactory inspection within 120 days before the application is processed. The location address on the application must match the licensed kitchen's location. Caution: thresholds vary across DBPR pages (1 year vs 18 months) — see open_questions.

requirements.fees: $624-$1,820/year by county population per Fla. Stat. s. 565.02(1)(b)-(f): county population over 100,000 = $1,820; 75,001-100,000 = $1,560; 50,001-75,000 = $1,300; 25,001-50,000 = $858; 25,000 or less = $624. forms.name: DBPR ABT-6001 - Application for New Alcoholic Beverage License (with detailed instructions)

requirements.notes: ABT checklist states the 4COP category covers 'Beer, Wine and Liquor Consumption on Premises' (on-premises consumption only, not package sales). Apply online via the myfloridalicense.com Online Services link or mail/hand-deliver to an ABT district office. Applicants must complete form ABT-6001; may be required to submit fingerprints (ABT ORI# FL920150Z via FDLE Livescan vendor list; out-of-state applicants request a fingerprint card from the division), certified arrest dispositions, moral-character mitigation, right of occupancy, premises sketch, zoning approval, health approval, FEIN/SSN, contracts, partner/officer/stockholder info, Secretary of State certificate of status, and Department of Revenue clearance. Note: new 4COP quota licenses can only be issued if the county has quota availability (see FL_DRAFT_ABT_0003); most buyers acquire an existing license by transfer (see FL_DRAFT_ABT_0004).

requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: A bona fide food service establishment wants a full-liquor on-premises license outside the county quota by meeting food-service criteria instead of buying a quota license.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 561.20(2)(a)4 (as amended by 2023 HB 639)

forms.name: DBPR ABT-6001 - Application for New Alcoholic Beverage License (with detailed instructions)

requirements.notes: Eligibility under s. 561.20(2)(a)4 as amended in 2023 (HB 639, effective 2023): a bona fide food service establishment with at least 2,000 sq ft of service area, equipped to serve meals to 120 persons at one time, at least 120 physical seats for patrons during operating hours, holding itself out as a restaurant, deriving at least 51% of gross food and beverage revenue from food and nonalcoholic beverages. (Prior to 2023 the thresholds were 2,500 sq ft / 150 persons; the 2020 statute text confirmed on flsenate.gov.) License may NOT operate as a package store and no liquor sales after food service/consumption hours have elapsed. The 51% test is measured over the first 60-day operating period and each 12-month period thereafter; failure = revocation or denial, and the disqualified person is ineligible for a subsequent SFS application for 120 days. SFS licenses are NOT movable to a new location - valid only on the premises where issued. ABT requires Division of Hotels and Restaurants approval for SFS applications. Annual fee: ABT's 2017 fact sheet (hosted third-party but sourced to ABT) listed $1,820; current fee chart PDF did not render during research - confirm on the ABT fee chart. ABT also publishes a General Laws of Local Application and Special Acts reference (GENLAWS.pdf) because local special acts in some counties set different SFS thresholds.

A new license is issued for each population increase of 7,500 residents above the April 1, 1999 baseline. Regardless of the cap, at least THREE licenses must be available in any county that approves liquor sales. Quota licenses are issued by the division subject to this limitation; when new quota capacity opens, ABT issues licenses via a drawing process (s. 561.19) - details not verified on an official source during this research. ABT publishes NO secondary-market price data; private sale prices are negotiated between parties and ABT does not set them.

requirements.agency: IRS
requirements.applies_when: You need an EIN to hire employees, operate a partnership or corporation, pay sales/excise taxes, or change business structure/ownership. If forming a corporation or LLC, form the entity with the Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz) before applying, or the EIN application may be delayed.
requirements.citation: IRS, 'Get an employer identification number' (irs.gov); 26 USC s. 6109 not independently verified
requirements.fees: Free. The IRS states you never have to pay a fee for an EIN and warns against websites that charge for one.

forms.name: Form SS-4, Application for Employer Identification Number (required for fax or mail filing)

requirements.notes: Online tool eligibility (all must be true): domestic organization formed in the US or US territories; principal place of business in the US or US territories; applicant is the responsible party or its authorized representative; has the responsible party's SSN or ITIN. Cannot apply online with an existing EIN (except government entities) or if principal place of business is outside the US (use phone/fax/mail). One EIN per responsible party per day. Session expires after 15 minutes of inactivity; the application cannot be saved mid-session. Availability (ET): Mon-Fri 6:00 a.m.-1:00 a.m. next day; Sat 6:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m.; Sun 6:00 p.m.-12:00 a.m.
requirements.timeline: Online: issued immediately after the application is approved. Fax and mail timelines: unverified on the fetched IRS page (third-party sources report ~4 business days by fax, ~4 weeks by mail).

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: A restaurant (non-construction industry) that employs four (4) or more employees, including business owners who are corporate officers or LLC members, must carry workers' compensation coverage. Non-construction sole proprietors or partners in a partnership are not employees unless they elect to be included on the policy (Form DWC-251).
requirements.citation: Florida Statutes ch. 440; s. 440.38 (securing compensation) not independently verified
requirements.fees: unverified (premiums set by licensed carriers; not published as a fixed schedule on the coverage page)

forms.name: Form DWC-251, Notice of Election of Coverage (for sole proprietors/partners electing coverage)

requirements.notes: The Division publishes a Proof of Coverage Database (dwcdataportal.fldfs.com), a Non-Compliance Referral database, and an Exemption Search for verifying coverage and reporting non-compliant employers. Contrast: construction employers need coverage with 1+ employees; agricultural employers at 6 regular or 12 seasonal workers (more than 30 days in a season / 45 days in a calendar year). Out-of-state employers working in Florida must obtain a Florida policy from a Florida-approved carrier with 'Florida' listed in Section 3A of the policy.
requirements.timeline: unverified (no statutory deadline published on the fetched coverage page; coverage must be in place once the employer meets the threshold)
requirements.title: Florida workers' compensation insurance — non-construction coverage rule

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: A business owner who is a corporate officer or LLC member in a non-construction business may opt out of coverage for themselves by meeting the Division's exemption requirements. The exemption applies to the individual filer only — the business must still carry coverage for all other employees (including the owner count toward the 4-employee threshold).
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 440.05 (not independently verified)
requirements.fees: unverified (Division reported collecting exemption fees in FY 2024/25 annual report; specific fee amounts not confirmed on fetched pages)

forms.name: Exemption application (electronic, via Division of Workers' Compensation)

requirements.notes: Verified on the Division's coverage page: 'Exemptions are available to business owners who opt out of the insurance coverage protections for themselves and who meet the requirements for an Exemption.' The 4-employee threshold is calculated including corporate officers/LLC members; an exempted officer still counts toward the 4-employee threshold for the business (per Division FAQ guidance published in secondary sources; exact online application URL not captured from fetched pages — needs confirmation).
requirements.timeline: unverified (Division reports processing 99.33% of online exemption applications within 10 business days of receipt in FY 2024/25)
requirements.title: Workers' compensation exemption for corporate officers / owners

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: Any employer required to secure workers' compensation coverage under Fla. Stat. ch. 440 that fails to do so. The Division (Bureau of Compliance) conducts onsite and virtual inspections; if noncompliant, the Division must issue a Stop-Work Order requiring the employer to cease all business operations.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 440.107 (2023 statute text as published by the Florida Senate)
requirements.fees: Penalty equal to 2 times the amount the employer would have paid in premium (approved manual rates applied to payroll) during the noncompliant period within the preceding 12-month period, or $1,000, whichever is greater; for employers with a prior stop-work order (or material payroll understatement/concealment) the preceding 24-month period is used. Plus $1,000 per day for each day of operations in violation of a stop-work order.
requirements.notes: Credit for initial premium payment: an employer not previously issued a stop-work order may receive a credit for the initial estimated annual workers' comp policy premium (with documentation) applied against the penalty; the $1,000 minimum applies even after the credit. The statute also provides for orders of conditional release, periodic payment agreements (the Division managed 2,536 PPAs totaling ~$24.9M outstanding as of 6/30/2025, per the DWC 2025 annual report), and stop-work orders binding successor entities. Note: older Florida statutes and many secondary sources cite '1.5 times the premium for the preceding 3-year period'; the 2023 statute text shows the 2x / 12-month (24-month for repeat offenders) formula. Flagged as a possible amendment — see open questions.
requirements.title: Penalties for failure to secure Florida workers' compensation coverage

requirements.agency: E-Verify / Florida
requirements.applies_when: Beginning July 1, 2023, a private employer with 25 or more employees must use the federal E-Verify system to verify the employment eligibility of each new employee within 3 business days after the first day the employee begins working for pay. Applies only to new hires (not retroactive). Employers with fewer than 25 employees verify via Form I-9 documentation instead and must retain a copy for at least 3 years.
requirements.fees: unverified (third-party sources report E-Verify itself is a free DHS/SSA service; not confirmed on the fetched official pages)

forms.name: Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification (federal; fallback if E-Verify unavailable for 3 business days)

requirements.notes: Enforcement by FloridaCommerce (formerly DEO). First determination of noncompliance: notice and 30 days to cure. Three failures in any 24-month period: $1,000 per day fine until compliance is proved; noncompliance is grounds for suspension of all licenses issued by a ch. 120 licensing agency until cured. FloridaCommerce, FDLE, the Attorney General, a State Attorney, or the Statewide Prosecutor may request the employer's verification documentation. Complaints may be sent to EVerifyCompliance@commerce.fl.gov.
requirements.timeline: Verify each new employee within 3 business days after the first day of work for pay. Employers required to use E-Verify must certify compliance on their first unemployment/reemployment-assistance tax return each calendar year. If the E-Verify system is unavailable for 3 business days, use Form I-9 and document the unavailability (screenshots each day, public announcement, or other recorded notice). Retain documentation for at least 3 years.
requirements.title: Florida E-Verify mandate for private employers with 25 or more employees

requirements.agency: E-Verify / Florida
requirements.applies_when: A Florida employer subject to the s. 448.095 E-Verify mandate (25+ employees) must first enroll in E-Verify before creating verification cases for new hires.

forms.name: E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) — electronically reviewed and signed during enrollment

requirements.notes: Per e-verify.gov, enrollment steps include: visit the enrollment website and accept terms; create a new company account via email activation link (one-time-use; enrollment completed in a single session); review the enrollment checklist; choose an access method (Employer, E-Verify Employer Agent, Corporate Administrator, or Web Services) by answering four guided questions; choose employer category (federal contractor w/ or w/o FAR clause, government, or none); then complete company details, NAICS code, hiring-site information, program administrator registration, and certification of information. A restaurant would select the standard 'Employer' access method with 'None of these categories apply.' Direct E-Verify enrollment URL (everify.uscis.gov/enroll) appeared only in secondary sources — not used as a citation URL.
requirements.timeline: unverified (enrollment itself is a one-time setup completed in a single online session; third-party sources report account activation can take up to ~3 weeks)
requirements.title: E-Verify employer enrollment process

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Any person or business organization acting as a contractor in Florida for work in a regulated category.
requirements.fees: Varies by license type; see fee requirements
requirements.notes: Two licensure paths: CERTIFIED — pass the state competency examination, work anywhere in the state (certified license numbers begin with C). REGISTERED — hold a local (county/city) certificate of competency and register with the state; practice only in the jurisdiction(s) that issued the local competency card (numbers begin with R). A new business wanting statewide operation needs certified licensure; a business staying in one locality may use the registered path if the locality still issues local competency licenses. Per s. 489.117, registered contractors may also practice in adjoining locales that accept the registration.
requirements.timeline: Board must approve or deny an application within 90 days; licenses are typically issued within two weeks after the board meeting in which the application was approved.
requirements.title: Contractor licensing required before doing business — certified vs registered

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Contracting for any activity requiring licensure under Ch. 489 Part I, i.e., any type of construction work.
requirements.notes: Division I license (Div I = paragraphs (a)-(c)). Services are unlimited as to type of work; may contract for and perform any work requiring licensure under Part I, except as expressly provided in s. 489.113. Division I licenses (general/building/residential) carry higher financial-stability thresholds (up to $20,000 net worth/cash/bonding by rule, s. 489.115(7)).
requirements.title: License category: General Contractor (CGC)

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Building commercial buildings or residential buildings no more than three stories tall, or non-structural remodeling/repair of any size building.
requirements.notes: Division I. Limited to construction of commercial and single-/multiple-dwelling residential buildings not exceeding three stories in height, plus accessory-use structures; or remodeling/repair/improvement of any size building if services do not affect structural members.
requirements.title: License category: Building Contractor (CBC)

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Building, remodeling, repairing, or improving one-, two-, or three-family residences not exceeding the statutory height limit.
requirements.notes: Division I. Limited to one-family, two-family, or three-family residences not exceeding two habitable stories above no more than one uninhabitable story, plus accessory-use structures.
requirements.title: License category: Residential Contractor (CRC)

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Contracting in a specialty trade rather than general/building/residential construction.
requirements.notes: Division II categories per CILB FAQ: sheet metal; roofing; air-conditioning (Classes A/B/C); mechanical; swimming pool/spa (commercial, residential, servicing); plumbing; underground utility and excavation; solar; and pollutant storage. In addition, certified specialty contractor licenses (created by CILB rulemaking, e.g., specialty structure, gypsum drywall, marine, glass and glazing, tower, building demolition, irrigation, industrial facilities, rooftop solar heating, structural masonry, structural steel, etc., plus pool specialties) are voluntary statewide licenses obtainable instead of a local specialty license. Division II financial-stability thresholds cap lower (up to $10,000 by rule, s. 489.115(7)).
requirements.title: License categories: Division II trades and certified specialty contractors

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Seeking a certified contractor license by examination.

forms.name: Florida contractor's examination application

requirements.notes: Must be 18 years old and of good moral character, plus one of: (1) baccalaureate degree from an accredited 4-year college in engineering, architecture, or building construction plus 1 year of proven experience in the category; or (2) at least 4 years of active experience as a skilled worker/apprentice or foreman, with at least 1 year as a foreman. Minimum 2,000 person-hours = full-time equivalency. Trade-knowledge exam exemption available for applicants with a building-construction baccalaureate degree and 3.0+ GPA (then only the Business and Finance exam is required).
requirements.title: Eligibility to sit for the certification examination

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Seeking a certified contractor license by examination.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 489.111; FAC Rule 61G4-16.009

forms.name: Florida contractor's examination application (via Professional Testing, Inc. / Pearson VUE)

requirements.notes: Open-book exams. Trade Knowledge, Project Management, and Contract Administration given the same day; Business/Finance exam is 6.5 hours. Computer-based exams (except Plumbing Trade Knowledge) administered by Pearson VUE at sites statewide, available at any time. Only failed sections must be retaken (61G4-16.009). Active CILB licensees adding a category are exempt from the Business/Finance portion. NASCLA-accredited general/building/residential exams plus the Florida Business and Finance exam and a Florida Building Code exam can support endorsement (Form DBPR CILB 10). Alternative path: hold an out-of-state license for 10+ years and apply for endorsement (2-hour Florida Building Code / wind mitigation course required for Division I and roofing).
requirements.timeline: All exam portions must be completed within 4 years of the first attempt; after 4 years all scores expire and the full exam must be retaken. Application for licensure must be made within 4 years of passing.
requirements.title: State contractor examination — format, sections, retakes

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Applying for initial certified licensure.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 489.111(2)(c); CILB FAQ

forms.name: Application for initial certified contractor's license

requirements.notes: Four years of field experience in the category of licensure, including at least one year of supervisory experience. Up to 3 years of any military service (DD214) or any accredited college credit hours may substitute; at least one year of supervisory construction experience in the licensed category is still required. Special experience required for general/building: demonstrate experience in 4 of 6 categories (foundations/slabs over 20,000 sq ft, masonry walls, steel erection, elevated slabs, column erection, formwork for structural reinforced concrete); for general contractors, at least one year of such experience must be new construction of structures of at least 4 stories.
requirements.title: Experience documentation — 4 years field + 1 year supervisory

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Applying for initial certification or registration, requesting a change of status, or qualifying a business entity.
requirements.notes: Submit a credit report from a nationally recognized credit agency showing a FICO-derived credit score of 660 or higher, with a public-records statement that local, state, and federal records were checked. If the score is below 660, applicant must complete a board-approved 14-hour financial responsibility and stability course. Proof of satisfaction of liens, judgments, and discharge of bankruptcy required where applicable. For business qualification, credit reports are required on the qualifying agent AND both the presently qualified and proposed qualified businesses. A financially responsible officer (FRO) model exists: if the qualifier lacks financial responsibility, the business must appoint an FRO, who must hold a $100,000 surety bond or irrevocable letter of credit payable to the CILB (letter of bondability not accepted). Statutory net-worth/cash/bonding guidelines are capped at $20,000 for Division I and $10,000 for Division II certificateholders.
requirements.title: Financial responsibility — credit report and FICO 660 / 14-hour course or bond

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Initial issuance and renewal of any certificate or registration; active licensees must maintain coverage at all times.
requirements.notes: Submit board-form affidavit attesting to workers' compensation coverage per Ch. 440, public liability, and property damage insurance in board-determined amounts. CILB-published minimums: general and building contractors $300,000 liability / $50,000 property damage; all other categories $100,000 liability / $25,000 property damage (or amounts set by board rule). Active licensees must maintain workers' comp coverage OR an exemption; applicants may state they will obtain the exemption within 30 days of licensure.
requirements.timeline: Affidavit of insurance required before issuance and at each renewal; workers' compensation exemption (if applicable) must be obtained within 30 days of becoming licensed.
requirements.title: Insurance — general liability, property damage, workers' compensation affidavit

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Applying for initial licensure or qualifying a construction business.
requirements.notes: Electronic fingerprints and criminal-history disclosure are required (application checklists list electronic fingerprints and supporting legal documentation). The board may not deny licensure based solely on a felony conviction or failure to provide proof of restoration of civil rights (s. 489.115(6)), but criminal history, good moral character, and financial stability are review factors; applicants with concerns may be placed on probationary status and required to appear before the board twice annually. Number, severity, recency of convictions and rehabilitation efforts are weighed individually.
requirements.title: Fingerprint-based background check and criminal history disclosure

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Operating as a corporation, partnership, LLC, or any business entity other than a sole proprietorship; or operating as an individual under a business name.
requirements.fees: Statutory cap: $50 initial application fee and $50 renewal fee to qualify a business organization

forms.name: Application for initial licensure qualifying a business (e.g., DBPR CILB 6-series by category)

requirements.notes: Contractors must qualify their construction business with their individual license; the license is issued in the qualifying agent's name with the business name noted on it. The qualifying agent must have supervisory authority and final approval over all construction affairs. Qualifying an additional business requires a separate application (e.g., DBPR CILB 7-H for an additional business) and triggers board appearance if the applicant owns under 20% or would qualify 3+ businesses. If a qualifying agent resigns/is fired, the company has 60 days to obtain another qualifier (temporary nonrenewable license available); if the qualifier dies, notify the board within 30 days. Certificates of Authority (qualified business licenses) have not been issued since October 1, 2009.
requirements.title: Qualifying agent — business must be qualified by a licensed contractor

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Submitting any application for initial certification or registration.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ss. 489.109(1)(a)-(c); DBPR CILB application instructions
requirements.fees: Initial certification: $245 if applying May 1 of an EVEN year through Aug 31 of an ODD year; $145 if applying Sept 1 of an ODD year through Apr 30 of an EVEN year. Statutory caps: certificate application fee ≤$150 (≤$350 combined with exam cost); certification and renewal fees ≤$250; registration application fee ≤$100; registration and renewal fees ≤$200.

forms.name: DBPR CILB 6-series / 7-H application forms (per category)

requirements.notes: Mail completed application, documentation, and fees to DBPR, 2601 Blair Stone Road, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0783. Applications are also available through DBPR Online Services. Note registered-contractor application fee windows differ (odd/even year cycle); published registration fee examples ($205/$105) were seen in a third-party mirror of the state form — confirm current fee windows on the official form before paying.
requirements.timeline: Board must approve or deny within 90 days of application; applications are typically sent to the first board meeting after receipt (board does not meet in December).
requirements.title: Application fees and where to file

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Every CILB license holder at each biennial renewal.
requirements.fees: Delinquent fee $250; inactive-status fee $50 (no fee to become inactive during a renewal period). Statutory caps: renewal ≤$250 (certified) / ≤$200 (registered); inactive renewal ≤$50.
requirements.notes: Renew by completing, signing, and forwarding the renewal application with fee; delinquency fees may not exceed the renewal fee. Licensees whose licenses were not renewed by expiration are expired (may not practice) — reactivation requires the reactivation application, fee, and CE for the preceding cycle. A null-and-void license (not renewed for an extended period) generally requires starting over, including retaking the exam; reinstatement applications (Form DBPR CILB 26, $100 fee) exist for illness/economic hardship cases at DBPR discretion. Additional $4 per application/renewal funds building-construction industry research/CE per s. 489.109(3).
requirements.timeline: Certified contractors renew August 31 of every EVEN-numbered year; registered contractors renew August 31 of every ODD-numbered year. Inactive licenses must still be renewed every two years.
requirements.title: Renewal cycle and renewal/delinquent/inactive fees

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: All active certified and registered contractors at each biennial renewal.
requirements.notes: 14 hours required, including at least 1 hour each in: Workplace Safety, Workers' Compensation, Business Practices, Advanced Module Building Code, and Laws and Rules. General, building, residential, roofing, specialty structure, and glass-and-glazing specialty contractors must also complete 1 hour of Wind Mitigation Methodology within the 14 hours; remainder are general credits. Reduced obligation for licenses issued mid-cycle: <12 months before renewal = no CE; 12-24 months = 7 hours general credits. Online courses available through providers designated C/I or I on the board's CE page. Core-course requirement was removed by the Legislature in 2009.
requirements.timeline: 14 hours due each 2-year renewal cycle (Aug 31 even years certified / odd years registered).
requirements.title: Continuing education — 14 hours per renewal cycle

requirements.agency: Construction Industry Licensing Board (DBPR)
requirements.applies_when: Any advertising, bidding, contracting, or permit application by a contractor or business.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 489.119(5); Fla. Stat. s. 489.127
requirements.notes: Every registered or certified contractor must display the license number on any building-permit application; offer of service; business proposal; bid; contract; advertisement (including websites); sign; and vehicles displaying the contractor/business name. Engaging in contracting without the required certificate or registration is prohibited and subject to cease-and-desist, noncriminal fines (up to $500; $250/day for continuing violations), and criminal penalties under s. 489.127. Work not requiring a state license: cabinets, countertops, paint, wallpaper, carpet, tile, window treatments; handyman jobs under $2,500 total construction cost that are casual/minor/inconsequential are exempt from state licensure (local rules may still apply).
requirements.title: Advertising and permit rules — license number display; no contracting without license

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: You operate in the construction industry and have one or more employees. Unlike the general rule (non-construction employers need 4+ employees, covered in round 1), ANY construction employer with 1+ employees must carry workers' compensation coverage — and owners count: corporate officers and LLC members are considered employees for this purpose unless they hold a valid Certificate of Election to be Exempt.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 440; Division of Workers' Compensation, Coverage Requirements page
requirements.fees: unverified (premiums set by licensed carriers; not published as a fixed schedule)
requirements.notes: Construction-only rule; builds on round 1 general findings. The Division lists which trades are 'construction industry' at Fla. Admin. Code 69L-6.021 (linked from the coverage page).
requirements.timeline: unverified (coverage must be in place once the employer meets the threshold; no statutory deadline published on the coverage page)
requirements.title: Workers' compensation — construction industry mandatory coverage (1+ employees)

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: A construction contractor subcontracts any part of its work. Before the subcontractor begins work, the contractor must verify the subcontractor has workers' compensation coverage (documentation requirements at Fla. Admin. Code 69L-6.032) — if not, the subcontractor's employees become the statutory employees of the contractor, and the contractor pays benefits for any work-related injury, illness, or fatality.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 440; Division of Workers' Compensation, Coverage Requirements page ('Contractors' section)
requirements.notes: This is the construction-specific operational duty — a general contractor cannot rely on a sub's promise of coverage; uninsured subs' workers legally become the contractor's employees.
requirements.timeline: Verification must occur BEFORE the subcontractor begins work on the project
requirements.title: Workers' compensation — construction contractor subcontractor-verification duty

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: A corporate officer of a construction business wants to be exempt from workers' comp coverage for themselves. Corporation must be registered and active with the Florida Division of Corporations; applicant must be listed as an officer in those records AND attest to minimum 10% ownership. Strictly limited: no more than three officers of a corporation or any group of affiliated corporations (including LLCs) may elect to be exempt.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 440.05; Division of Workers' Compensation, Construction Industry exemption page
requirements.fees: $50.00 application fee (non-construction exemptions are free). The Division warns service fees may also apply.

forms.name: Certificate of Election to be Exempt — online application (Division of Workers' Compensation)

requirements.notes: Compare round 1 non-construction rules: no fee and no limit on number of exempt corporate officers. Construction is far stricter (3-officer cap, $50 fee). Applicant cannot be affiliated with an ACTIVE Stop Work Order or Working in Violation, and cannot have an associated insufficient payment.
requirements.timeline: Exemptions valid for 2 years; effective/expiration dates listed on the Certificate. Renewal requires a valid state driver's license not expired more than 30 days at submission.
requirements.title: Workers' compensation construction exemption — corporate officers (max 3, $50 fee)

requirements.agency: Florida Division of Workers' Compensation
requirements.applies_when: An LLC member of a construction business wants to be exempt from workers' comp coverage for themselves. LLC must be registered and active with the Florida Division of Corporations; applicant must attest to minimum 10% ownership. Limit: no more than three members of an LLC or any group of affiliated LLCs (including corporations) may elect to be exempt.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 440.05; Division of Workers' Compensation, Construction Industry exemption page
requirements.fees: $50.00 application fee per applicant; service fees may also apply

forms.name: Certificate of Election to be Exempt — online application (Division of Workers' Compensation)

requirements.notes: Compare non-construction LLC rule: up to 10 members exempt, no fee. Exemption is issued to the individual, not the business — a separate application per person per entity. A valid state driver's license is required to obtain or renew.
requirements.timeline: Valid for 2 years; renew before expiration. Customer service: (850) 413-1609, wc_exemption@myfloridacfo.com
requirements.title: Workers' compensation construction exemption — LLC members (max 3, $50 fee)

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources (RER), Construction Trades Qualifying Board
requirements.applies_when: You do contracting work in Miami-Dade County in a trade category that is NOT covered by a State of Florida certified contractor license. State-certified contractors need NO further county license (state preempts local licensing; they only register with the County Building Department). County Certificates of Competency cover local-only categories issued under Chapter 10 of the Miami-Dade County Code — general/building/residential contractors and specialty trades (electrical, plumbing, mechanical, roofing, swimming pool, maintenance, and building specialties).
requirements.citation: Miami-Dade County Code ch. 10; s. 163.211, F.S. (HB 735 preemption, effective July 1, 2021)
